sections.title: Storage + constructor (and why `quiltId` isn't immutable)
sections.key_moment: Solidity does not allow `immutable` on `string` (or any dynamic-size type) — `quiltId` and `aggregator` are plain storage variables, conventionally written-once by the constructor. The CONVENTION (vs. the language) is what guarantees immutability of `quiltId`; the absence of any setter is the proof. For `aggregator`, the deliberate `setAggregator` setter exists as a sunset knob — the language can't help you here, the design intent is the contract.

sections.title: Self-mint with sequential ids + maxSupply cap
sections.key_moment: `tokenId = _nextTokenId++;` (post-increment) — the local `tokenId` gets the CURRENT value (1 on first mint), then storage gets bumped to 2 for the next call. Pre-increment would skip id `1` and start at `2`. Combined with the `<=` cap (not `<`), this produces a half-open-then-closed window that mints exactly `[1, maxSupply]` and rejects the (maxSupply+1)-th call. One character matters in both places.

sections.title: `tokenURI` — building the deterministic aggregator URL
sections.key_moment: `tokenURI` is a PURE STRING-CONCAT — no SLOAD other than the two storage strings, no mapping lookup, no per-token state. The url shape `<aggregator>/v1/blobs/by-quilt-id/<quiltId>/<tokenId>.json` is uniform across every token; the only thing that differs per token is the decimal id. That's what collapses 10 000 token URIs into TWO storage strings + a one-line view function — and what makes off-chain URL derivation possible without any RPC at all.

sections.title: `setAggregator` — the sunset-migration knob
sections.key_moment: `setAggregator` is owner-only and the ONLY mutable storage slot after deployment. The reason it exists at all: Walrus aggregator hosts are commodity HTTPS endpoints, and any specific host might sunset. Because Walrus blobs are content-addressed, pointing at a different aggregator returns the SAME bytes — only the URL prefix changes. The migration is one transaction, costs no re-pinning, and surfaces as an `AggregatorUpdated` event for indexers to follow.
